root_cause.text: The TTLM parser unconditionally reads a link mapping presence indicator byte without first checking if the default link map control flag is set, causing out-of-bounds buffer access when a default mapping is used.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a conditional check `if (!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP))` before reading `*pos` and incrementing the position pointer. The original code at lines 6193-6194 always executed `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` regardless of whether the element contained link mapping data. According to the CVE description, when a default mapping is used, the TTLM element does not contain a link mapping presence indicator, so the original code would read one byte beyond the end of the element.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally reads the link_map_presence byte from the buffer without first checking if the IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEFAULT_LINK_MAP flag is set in the control field. According to the TTLM packet structure, this field should only be present and read when the default link map control flag is set. Reading it unconditionally causes out-of-bounds buffer access when processing packets with default link mapping, as the expected buffer layout differs from what the code assumes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability root cause describes an unconditional read of a link mapping presence indicator byte without checking if the default link map control flag is set. In the `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l()` function shown in this commit, the code correctly handles this: (1) Line 31 reads `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` unconditionally, but (2) Line 50-52 checks `if (control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP)` and returns early with `ttlm_info->map = 0xffff; return 0;` BEFORE attempting to use `link_map_presence` for further parsing. (3) Only after this check passes does the code proceed to line 67 where it validates `if (link_map_presence != 0xff)`. This early return when the default link map flag is set prevents out-of-bounds access. The function is moved earlier in the file (before line 6161) in this commit, and the logic itself contains the proper fix by checking the control flag before using the link_map_presence value for buffer access operations.
